sanctions.metadataDescription: How 6529 follows sanctions laws: the places where 6529.io isn't available, the official lists of wallet addresses it checks, and the list itself.
sanctions.title: How 6529 follows sanctions laws
sanctions.lead: 6529.io is run by 6529 Collection LLC, a company based in the United States. Sanctions laws limit where we can offer the site and which wallets can use it. This page explains how we apply them and lists every wallet address we check.
sanctions.leadNote: We would love to welcome everyone. These limits come from the law, not from a judgment about anyone reading this.
sanctions.contents.label: On this page
sanctions.places.title: Places
sanctions.places.intro: The United States applies comprehensive sanctions to a few places. 6529.io isn't available in them:
sanctions.places.crimea: The Crimea region of Ukraine, including Sevastopol
sanctions.places.donetskLuhansk: The Donetsk and Luhansk regions of Ukraine
sanctions.places.detectionTitle: How we tell where you are
sanctions.places.detection: We estimate your location from your internet connection: your IP address and the network it belongs to. The estimate isn't always right.
sanctions.places.vpn: If you use a VPN, or a network that routes you through one of these places, the site may not load even if you are somewhere else. Try a different connection. If you are travelling, the site works again once you have left.
sanctions.places.contact: Think we got it wrong? Email {email} and we'll take a look.
sanctions.wallets.title: Wallet addresses
sanctions.wallets.intro: Some governments publish the crypto wallet addresses of people and organizations they have sanctioned. We collect the Ethereum-style addresses (starting 0x) from these official lists:
sanctions.wallets.ruleAnyList: A listing on any one of these lists is enough.
sanctions.wallets.ruleProfile: If any wallet in a 6529 profile is listed, the whole profile is affected, including the profile's other consolidated wallets.
sanctions.wallets.ruleDelegation: A delegation to or from a listed wallet carries no rights. The other wallet is not blocked because of it.
sanctions.wallets.ruleBrowse: A listed profile can still browse 6529.io while signed out. It can't sign in, post, vote, give rep or NIC, delegate, mint, subscribe or make payments.
sanctions.wallets.ruleFrequency: We rebuild the list from the official sources every day. When an authority removes an address, it leaves our list at the next rebuild.
sanctions.wallets.appeal: Email {email} with the wallet address and your profile, and we'll review the exact listing. If we read an address from a list by mistake, we correct it and publish the correction.
sanctions.wallets.appealDelisting: If an address really is on a list, only the authority that listed it can remove it. For the US list, OFAC explains {link}.
sanctions.list.title: The list
sanctions.list.intro: These are the wallet addresses we check, grouped by the authority that published them. The list contains official public data only.
sanctions.list.previewNote: This is a preview snapshot built on {date}. A list rebuilt and signed every day will replace it.
sanctions.list.verify: The list is a single file. Its SHA-256 hash and IPFS content ID let anyone confirm they have exactly the same bytes, and anyone can rebuild it from the official files with our open builder.
sanctions.list.noAddresses: This list currently includes no wallet addresses.
sanctions.list.lapsedIntro: These Israeli seizure orders have passed their validity date, so we don't enforce them. An address here may still appear on another list above.
sanctions.footer: This page shows official public sanctions data. It is not legal advice, and it may be out of date between rebuilds.
